title.narrative: CSSU002.5 SSU JR 2024-2026 Member

description.narrative: Goals: 1. Vulnerable people who experience multi-sectoral severity levels of 4 and 5 have reduced morbidity and mortality through equitable and dignified access to critical cross-sectoral essential services to meet their needs. 2. Vulnerable people are exposed to fewer protection threats and incidents, and those who are exposed have access to safe, tailored, timely and dignified access to appropriate services through integrated and inclusive humanitarian action. 3. Vulnerable people withstand and recover from shocks, have their resilience to shocks and stresses built, and seek solutions that respect their rights.

comment.narrative: AAP roles in Year 1, Year 2 & Year 3 - Through its AAP system, ACROSS will carefully collect input on this and make necessary changes. - Organize Project Management Committee and CAC meetings. - Collect feedback and respond to complaints from beneficiaries or non-beneficiaries. - conducting, and analyzing the accountability assessments. - Participate in translation of accountability materials into local language. - Prepares regular reports to be able to share the feedback and responses accordingly. - Actively participate in actual ideas for programme design and/or how to improve present execution. - Participate in production and distribution of Child-Friendly AAP materials to increase children's engagement. - sensitizing children and parents to the roles of children in feedback systems. - Communication and transparency - Formation of Child-Led Accountability Committees - Translation of AAP Materials to Applicable Visual and Audio - Participate in production and distribution of visibility materials for sensitization and training. - Procure100 DAPs each year for awareness raising. GAM activities in Year 1, Year 2 & Year 3 - Provision of Soap, Masks, and hand sanitizers for workshop participants. - Production and distribution of visibility materials. - Conduct 100 gender awareness campaigns. - Support to cultural music dance groups to create gender awareness.

description.narrative: Participation is defined as the involvement of crisis-affected people in one or more phases of the programme: assessment, design, implementation, monitoring or evaluation. title.narrative: Formal education (EDU-I1)
Number of boys and girls that access safe, quality learning opportunities (formal education)

description.narrative: Quality implies but is not limited to: 1) a safe learning environment, 2) competent and well-trained teachers who are knowledgeable in the subject matter, 3) adequate materials for teaching and learning, 4) participatory methods of instruction and 5) reasonable class sizes. Especially in complex emergencies this should take into account a psycho-social dimension. Safe implies: people’s physical and personal wellbeing and integrity as well as to their freedom from physical, environmental, social, spiritual, political, emotional and psychological harm.

comment.narrative:
Protection and MHPSS campaigns: 1. Organizing 12 child-led campaigns with 6 in Tonj North of Warrap State and in 6 in Pibor of Greater Pibor Administrative Area (GPAA) using the Boruboru campaign approach. description.narrative: 1) Preventive measure must be built on a thorough analysis of the risks and should - as much as possible - be designed to provide concrete changes in the short/medium term. title.narrative: Protection information dissemination (PRO-I5)
Number of persons with increased/appropriate information on relevant rights and/or entitlements

description.narrative: 1) Protection information dissemination refers to provision of information as opposed to actual training or capacity building on protection; as such this will normally target larger numbers than capacity building, and will not involve testing of increased knowledge.2) Relevant rights and entitlements must be defined and should be closely linked to actual risks faced be the targeted group as a result of the crisis.3) Entitlements refers (but is not limited to) availability and accesibility of services (both provided by humanitarian agencies and other actors).4) In activity description field the target group of dissemination (population/authorities/AFs/AGs, etc.) should be clarified.5) In activity description field define focus of information (Rights and access to services awareness, including child-specific measures, Sensitisation campaigns/Risk awareness; IHL/IHRL dissemination).6) Number of persons must be disaggregated by age and sex at reporting stage.

title.narrative: Child Protection (PRO-I15)
Number of children that received support specified to their needs

description.narrative:
1) This indicator covers response to children (girls and boys under 18). 2) Appropriate response is defined as the provision of comprehensive services/assistance based on a thorough analysis of the risks faced by persons. The protection outcome of the response must be well defined. Relevant SOPs (including functional Referral Mechanism) should be followed. 3) Use the activity description field to to describe what services (medical, MHPSS, legal, security, etc.), as well as SOPs are in place. Activities can include psychosocial support to children, Child Friendly Spaces and support to parents to fulfill their protection responsibilities towards their children. 4) Number of persons must be disaggregated by sex at reporting stage.5) If action also includes prevention activities, please describe this within the activity under this indicator.
If relevant, please specify in the activity description your target population, for example child soldiers.
